newsitem.title: FRANCE: French budget minister details audit findings.
newsitem.headline: French budget minister details audit findings.

text.p: France's 1997 public deficit is running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product instead of 3.0 percent forecast last year by the previous government, Budget Minister Christian Sautter said on Monday.

He told a news conference that an audit by two senior Court of Auditors officials found the central government budget deficit was running at 312-322 billion francs, 27-37 billion francs higher than budgeted.
The government was facing a tax shortfall this year of 15-15 billion francs and a public spending overshoot of 12-20 billion francs, Sautter said.
In addition, he said the welfare deficit in the main social security fund was running at 35-38 billion francs, compared with the 30.4 billion francs target set in the Social Security Finance Act.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told the same news conference that France must meet the Maastricht treaty budget deficit criterion of three percent of gross domestic product in 1997 to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
He also said economic growth in 1997 would be in line with expectations after a worse-than-expected first half. The previous conservative government had forecast 1997 GDP growth of 2.3 percent.
